output.text: Content creator Bea Borres breaks her silence amid the mixed reactions to her reunion with her ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada. Bea also playfully said that reuniting with her ex would help her earn money for their daughter, Victoria Hope. Despite their apparent boundaries, however, some fans still felt the kilig vibes between the former couple. Others, including Bea's close friend Andrea Brillantes, disagreed with the netizens' excitement over the ex-couple. READ: Andrea Brillantes on Bea Borres-Meray Yamada ship: 'Lahat kayo kinikilig, pwes ako hindi' Amid the reactions, Bea shared her thoughts on the hate comments circulating online. "Why are you guys mad at me!," she wrote. "Atleast I'm not accepting online sugal 😒 Mag clout chase nalang ako 😒 It's my content, just block me nalang if you think i'm tanga!!!!" The influencer also added in the comments, "If I promote sugal diba you'll bash me rin naman, go kanya-kanya na 'tong hustle." The following day, Bea Borres continued sharing content featuring Meray. Titled "Gatasan Serye," the new video showed Bea and Baby Hopea watching Meray play basketball. The influencer noted how much her daughter enjoyed cheering for her dad, while she continued to maintain her playful distance from her ex. Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple. READ: Bea Borres not worried taking on responsibility as a single parent Bea Borres previously revealed that they had broken up before she publicly announced her pregnancy last year. output.title: VERA FILES FACT SHEET: ‘Supercharged’ na mga mamamahayag na Filipino
output.description: Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Filipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno.

text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno. Tatlumpu’t apat (humigit-kumulang 75%) ang mga reklamong may kinalaman sa cyber libel na mapaparusahan sa ilalim ng Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at ang 10 ay libel sa ilalim ng Revised Penal Code. output.title: From monarchy to Islamic rule to war in Iran: A personal account (Part 1)
output.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. articles.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. articles.title: VERA FILES FACT SHEET: ‘Supercharged’ na mga mamamahayag na Filipino
articles.description: Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Filipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno.

text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno. Tatlumpu’t apat (humigit-kumulang 75%) ang mga reklamong may kinalaman sa cyber libel na mapaparusahan sa ilalim ng Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at ang 10 ay libel sa ilalim ng Revised Penal Code. articles.title: From monarchy to Islamic rule to war in Iran: A personal account (Part 1)
articles.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. articles.title: Bea Borres co-parenting daughter with ex's mother
articles.description: Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Content creator Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother. Borres was the guest on the May 8, 2026 episode of "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" which served as a Mother's Day special ahead of May's second Sunday. A majority of the episode revolved around Borres laying out her pregnancy experience, including how she and Yamada got together as well as how they broke up while carrying their child. Boy asked Borres if she was co-parenting with Yamada, whom the content creator humorously referred to as her "baby daddy," and Borres answered Yamada's mother Imelda "Mhel" Pechera was co-parenting with her. "Wala akong masabi kay Tita. Tita, if you're watching, napakabait mo... pero 'yung anak mo talaga..." Borres quipped. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? I'm just choosing myself, the way he chose himself," she pointed out. The episode ended with the titular "Fast Talk" segment after Borres prayed her daughter grows up God-fearing, kind, grounded, healthy, and successful in life, and for herself the ability to heal. — Video from GMA Network's YouTube channel RELATED: Never force: Elisse Joson advises fellow moms to let kids open up naturally Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. articles.title: VERA FILES FACT SHEET: ‘Supercharged’ na mga mamamahayag na Filipino
articles.description: Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Filipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno.

text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno. Tatlumpu’t apat (humigit-kumulang 75%) ang mga reklamong may kinalaman sa cyber libel na mapaparusahan sa ilalim ng Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at ang 10 ay libel sa ilalim ng Revised Penal Code. articles.title: From monarchy to Islamic rule to war in Iran: A personal account (Part 1)
articles.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. articles.title: Bea Borres reunites with ex Meray Yamada for content
articles.description: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content.
articles.text: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content. In a YouTube vlog titled "Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno," Bea inserted a short clip toward the latter part of the video, where she let Meray try the cake she baked. According to Bea, she purposely included Meray in the vlog to drive online engagement, which could then generate income. The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope. “I’ll just milk him for all he’s worth,” Bea said in Filipino. “You don't want to give me money? Well, engagement is high whenever I'm with you, so I'll just milk this for all it's worth,” she added. In the video, Bea spoon-fed Meray some of the cake she made, which she said could cause a fight with his other women. “You ruined my peace when I was pregnant, and you have a lot of women, so this act is for you to fight with them since karma takes so long to catch up,” she said. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025. That same month, she shared a sonogram and revealed that she is having a baby girl . In January, Bea revealed that she had given birth to Victoria Hope, or Hopea , in December 2025. In August, she returned to school at the Ateneo de Manila University . —Hermes Joy Tunac/JCB GMA News

articles.title: Bea Borres reacts to criticism over video reunion with ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada
articles.description: Bea Borres defends vlogging with ex Meray Yamada, notes she doesn't promote online gambling.
articles.text: Content creator Bea Borres breaks her silence amid the mixed reactions to her reunion with her ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada. Recently, the celebrity mom met up with Meray for what she jokingly described as a "clout-chasing" move for her vlog. Bea also playfully said that reuniting with her ex would help her earn money for their daughter, Victoria Hope. Despite their apparent boundaries, however, some fans still felt the kilig vibes between the former couple. Others, including Bea's close friend Andrea Brillantes, disagreed with the netizens' excitement over the ex-couple. READ: Andrea Brillantes on Bea Borres-Meray Yamada ship: 'Lahat kayo kinikilig, pwes ako hindi' Amid the reactions, Bea shared her thoughts on the hate comments circulating online. "Why are you guys mad at me!," she wrote. "Atleast I'm not accepting online sugal 😒 Mag clout chase nalang ako 😒 It's my content, just block me nalang if you think i'm tanga!!!!" The influencer also added in the comments, "If I promote sugal diba you'll bash me rin naman, go kanya-kanya na 'tong hustle." The following day, Bea Borres continued sharing content featuring Meray. Titled "Gatasan Serye," the new video showed Bea and Baby Hopea watching Meray play basketball. The influencer noted how much her daughter enjoyed cheering for her dad, while she continued to maintain her playful distance from her ex. Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple. READ: Bea Borres not worried taking on responsibility as a single parent Bea Borres previously revealed that they had broken up before she publicly announced her pregnancy last year. article.description: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content.
article.text: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content. In a YouTube vlog titled "Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno," Bea inserted a short clip toward the latter part of the video, where she let Meray try the cake she baked. According to Bea, she purposely included Meray in the vlog to drive online engagement, which could then generate income. The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope. “I’ll just milk him for all he’s worth,” Bea said in Filipino. “You don't want to give me money? Well, engagement is high whenever I'm with you, so I'll just milk this for all it's worth,” she added. In the video, Bea spoon-fed Meray some of the cake she made, which she said could cause a fight with his other women. “You ruined my peace when I was pregnant, and you have a lot of women, so this act is for you to fight with them since karma takes so long to catch up,” she said. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025. That same month, she shared a sonogram and revealed that she is having a baby girl . In January, Bea revealed that she had given birth to Victoria Hope, or Hopea , in December 2025. In August, she returned to school at the Ateneo de Manila University . —Hermes Joy Tunac/JCB GMA News

article.text: Content creator Bea Borres breaks her silence amid the mixed reactions to her reunion with her ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada. Recently, the celebrity mom met up with Meray for what she jokingly described as a "clout-chasing" move for her vlog. Bea also playfully said that reuniting with her ex would help her earn money for their daughter, Victoria Hope. Despite their apparent boundaries, however, some fans still felt the kilig vibes between the former couple. Others, including Bea's close friend Andrea Brillantes, disagreed with the netizens' excitement over the ex-couple. READ: Andrea Brillantes on Bea Borres-Meray Yamada ship: 'Lahat kayo kinikilig, pwes ako hindi' Amid the reactions, Bea shared her thoughts on the hate comments circulating online. "Why are you guys mad at me!," she wrote. "Atleast I'm not accepting online sugal 😒 Mag clout chase nalang ako 😒 It's my content, just block me nalang if you think i'm tanga!!!!" The influencer also added in the comments, "If I promote sugal diba you'll bash me rin naman, go kanya-kanya na 'tong hustle." The following day, Bea Borres continued sharing content featuring Meray. Titled "Gatasan Serye," the new video showed Bea and Baby Hopea watching Meray play basketball. The influencer noted how much her daughter enjoyed cheering for her dad, while she continued to maintain her playful distance from her ex. Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple. READ: Bea Borres not worried taking on responsibility as a single parent Bea Borres previously revealed that they had broken up before she publicly announced her pregnancy last year. article.title: VERA FILES FACT SHEET: ‘Supercharged’ na mga mamamahayag na Filipino
article.description: Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Filipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno.

text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno. Tatlumpu’t apat (humigit-kumulang 75%) ang mga reklamong may kinalaman sa cyber libel na mapaparusahan sa ilalim ng Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at ang 10 ay libel sa ilalim ng Revised Penal Code. article.title: From monarchy to Islamic rule to war in Iran: A personal account (Part 1)
article.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. article.title: Bea Borres co-parenting daughter with ex's mother
article.description: Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Content creator Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother. Borres was the guest on the May 8, 2026 episode of "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" which served as a Mother's Day special ahead of May's second Sunday. A majority of the episode revolved around Borres laying out her pregnancy experience, including how she and Yamada got together as well as how they broke up while carrying their child. Boy asked Borres if she was co-parenting with Yamada, whom the content creator humorously referred to as her "baby daddy," and Borres answered Yamada's mother Imelda "Mhel" Pechera was co-parenting with her. "Wala akong masabi kay Tita. Tita, if you're watching, napakabait mo... pero 'yung anak mo talaga..." Borres quipped. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? I'm just choosing myself, the way he chose himself," she pointed out. The episode ended with the titular "Fast Talk" segment after Borres prayed her daughter grows up God-fearing, kind, grounded, healthy, and successful in life, and for herself the ability to heal. — Video from GMA Network's YouTube channel RELATED: Never force: Elisse Joson advises fellow moms to let kids open up naturally Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. article.title: Nag-abot alang sa content
article.description: Nagkita pag-usab atubangan sa camera ang aktres ug content creator nga si Bea Borres ug iyang ex-boyfriend nga si Meray Yamada alang sa usa ka online content.
article.text: CEBU, Philippines — Nagkita pag-usab atubangan sa camera ang aktres ug content creator nga si Bea Borres ug iyang ex-boyfriend nga si Meray Yamada alang sa usa ka online content. Sa YouTube vlog nga “Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno,” gipakita ni Bea ang mubo nga video clip diin iyang gipatilaw si Meray sa hinimo niya nga cake.Suma pa ni Bea, gituyo niyang ilakip si Meray sa vlog aron madugangan ang online engagement ug mokita siya niini.Aduna na’y anak sila Bea ug Meray nga ginganlan og Hope . Gipasidunggan ni Negros Occidental 3rd District Rep. Javier Benitez ang Pinoy talents sa global stage, lakip na ang P-pop groups nga BINI ug SB19. Gihimo ni Benitez ang pagdayeg atol sa iyang pakigpulong sa mga kawani sa House of Representatives sa niaging adlaw, isip kabahin sa pagtimaan sa Philippine Creative Industries Month. Giawhag usab sa magbabalaod ang mga personnel sa Kamara nga suportahan ang lokal nga musika. Miangkon ang OPM singer nga si Jed Madela nga nabantayan na niya ang kakapoy samtang nag-perform sa entablado tungod sa iyang pagkatigulang. Matud niya, naningkamot siya karon nga maminusan ang timbang ug mahimong mas aktibo aron mapadayon ang iyang kusog sa pag-perform. articles.title: Bea Borres reunites with ex Meray Yamada for content
articles.description: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content.
articles.text: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content. In a YouTube vlog titled "Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno," Bea inserted a short clip toward the latter part of the video, where she let Meray try the cake she baked. According to Bea, she purposely included Meray in the vlog to drive online engagement, which could then generate income. The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope. “I’ll just milk him for all he’s worth,” Bea said in Filipino. “You don't want to give me money? Well, engagement is high whenever I'm with you, so I'll just milk this for all it's worth,” she added. In the video, Bea spoon-fed Meray some of the cake she made, which she said could cause a fight with his other women. “You ruined my peace when I was pregnant, and you have a lot of women, so this act is for you to fight with them since karma takes so long to catch up,” she said. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025. That same month, she shared a sonogram and revealed that she is having a baby girl . In January, Bea revealed that she had given birth to Victoria Hope, or Hopea , in December 2025. In August, she returned to school at the Ateneo de Manila University . —Hermes Joy Tunac/JCB GMA News

articles.text: Content creator Bea Borres breaks her silence amid the mixed reactions to her reunion with her ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada. Recently, the celebrity mom met up with Meray for what she jokingly described as a "clout-chasing" move for her vlog. Bea also playfully said that reuniting with her ex would help her earn money for their daughter, Victoria Hope. Despite their apparent boundaries, however, some fans still felt the kilig vibes between the former couple. Others, including Bea's close friend Andrea Brillantes, disagreed with the netizens' excitement over the ex-couple. READ: Andrea Brillantes on Bea Borres-Meray Yamada ship: 'Lahat kayo kinikilig, pwes ako hindi' Amid the reactions, Bea shared her thoughts on the hate comments circulating online. "Why are you guys mad at me!," she wrote. "Atleast I'm not accepting online sugal 😒 Mag clout chase nalang ako 😒 It's my content, just block me nalang if you think i'm tanga!!!!" The influencer also added in the comments, "If I promote sugal diba you'll bash me rin naman, go kanya-kanya na 'tong hustle." The following day, Bea Borres continued sharing content featuring Meray. Titled "Gatasan Serye," the new video showed Bea and Baby Hopea watching Meray play basketball. The influencer noted how much her daughter enjoyed cheering for her dad, while she continued to maintain her playful distance from her ex. Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple. READ: Bea Borres not worried taking on responsibility as a single parent Bea Borres previously revealed that they had broken up before she publicly announced her pregnancy last year. articles.title: Bea Borres co-parenting daughter with ex's mother
articles.description: Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Content creator Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother. Borres was the guest on the May 8, 2026 episode of "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" which served as a Mother's Day special ahead of May's second Sunday. A majority of the episode revolved around Borres laying out her pregnancy experience, including how she and Yamada got together as well as how they broke up while carrying their child. Boy asked Borres if she was co-parenting with Yamada, whom the content creator humorously referred to as her "baby daddy," and Borres answered Yamada's mother Imelda "Mhel" Pechera was co-parenting with her. "Wala akong masabi kay Tita. Tita, if you're watching, napakabait mo... pero 'yung anak mo talaga..." Borres quipped. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? I'm just choosing myself, the way he chose himself," she pointed out. The episode ended with the titular "Fast Talk" segment after Borres prayed her daughter grows up God-fearing, kind, grounded, healthy, and successful in life, and for herself the ability to heal. — Video from GMA Network's YouTube channel RELATED: Never force: Elisse Joson advises fellow moms to let kids open up naturally Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. articles.text: CEBU, Philippines — Nagkita pag-usab atubangan sa camera ang aktres ug content creator nga si Bea Borres ug iyang ex-boyfriend nga si Meray Yamada alang sa usa ka online content. Sa YouTube vlog nga “Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno,” gipakita ni Bea ang mubo nga video clip diin iyang gipatilaw si Meray sa hinimo niya nga cake.Suma pa ni Bea, gituyo niyang ilakip si Meray sa vlog aron madugangan ang online engagement ug mokita siya niini.Aduna na’y anak sila Bea ug Meray nga ginganlan og Hope . Gipasidunggan ni Negros Occidental 3rd District Rep. Javier Benitez ang Pinoy talents sa global stage, lakip na ang P-pop groups nga BINI ug SB19. Gihimo ni Benitez ang pagdayeg atol sa iyang pakigpulong sa mga kawani sa House of Representatives sa niaging adlaw, isip kabahin sa pagtimaan sa Philippine Creative Industries Month. Giawhag usab sa magbabalaod ang mga personnel sa Kamara nga suportahan ang lokal nga musika. Miangkon ang OPM singer nga si Jed Madela nga nabantayan na niya ang kakapoy samtang nag-perform sa entablado tungod sa iyang pagkatigulang. Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files.

Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon.
In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room.
I grew up in Tehran, Iran.
My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old.
For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.
My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier.
Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits.
I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman.
I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities.
We were an expat family.
The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans.
We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits.
It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays.
We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz.
We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little.
The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning.
We all knew each other.
Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain.
Fronting the courtyard was the ground floor unit of the family of lawyer and career diplomat now assigned as ambassador to Greeece, Giovanni Palec.
His father was my Papa’s longtime friend and colleague in Vietnam and then in Iran Air.
Like my sister and I, Giovy and his three siblings also attended Community School.

Students in Community School came from different countries whose parents were also expats assigned to Iran (diplomats, country managers and foreign company executives as well as Christian missionaries) or belonged to wealthy, elite Iranian families who could afford the pricey tuition.
Many of its graduates were accepted in top universities in the U.S., Canada, Europe and other parts of the world.

Later on, I learned that the highly decorated Army Gen. Norman Schwarzkopf, Commander-in-Chief of the U.S. Central Command of Operation Desert Storm in the 1990 Gulf War, was a student at Community School in the 1940s.
He led the allied coalition that drove Iraqi forces out of Kuwait which Saddam Hussein had invaded.
Former U.S. Ambassador to the Philippines Francis Ricciardone was an English teacher at Community School.
His wife was our school nurse.
The envoy was Giovy’s teacher along with several other Filipinos students.
At a welcome reception for Ricciardone, a Middle East expert, when he first arrived in Manila in January 2002, he said we were the first Filipinos he had ever met.
At a reunion the ambassador hosted for us in his residence, Giovy recalled how he and his classmates were reprimanded for plagiarism by Ricciardone on an assignment to write a haiku.
He said they all scrambled to the library to copy what they figured was the most obscure poem that had the 17 syllables of a Japanese haiku.
They got caught.
At the reunion, Giovy asked his former teacher if he knew all the haikus of the world.
Ricciardone smiled and replied, “Just about.”
Giovy and his pals never stood a chance.
The former British ambassador to the Philippines, Asif Ahmad, was a classmate of my brother.
A nephew of the Shah was also in his class.
Growing up, my friends and I hung out together: watched English movies at Cinema Goldis, plays and concerts at the cultural center of the Iran-America Society;
we went skating at the Ice Palace, ate hamburgers at Moby Dick outlets.
On weekends, there was hiking in the Alborz Mountains or swimming in the pool at the Thai Embassy in the summer and skiing in Abali or Dizin in the winter.

There were sleepovers, invites to the vacation homes of classmates along the Caspian Sea, school field trips to Isfahan , Persepolis and other key cities of what was the great Persian Empire of a bygone era.

We jumped over bonfires before Nowruz , the Iranian new year, believed to cleanse the body of bad luck and bring good health and happiness, celebrated the Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan, the one-month fasting and prayers of Muslims.
It was in the home of my junior high best friend, daughter of a consul at the American Embassy, that I first learned that avocados could be an ingredient in a vegetable salad.
Like all Filipinos, I was used to eating avocados mixed with sugar and milk.
In the home of another classmate, I had my first orange juice squeezed from the actual fruit and not from powder in a jar like we had in our house.
This was the Iran I knew: peaceful, fun and free, tolerant of diversity, exotic and cultured, modern and traditional all at the same time.
It was years later that I realized that we had lived in a bubble.

Sheltered and oblivious to what was happening outside the thick walls of the closed campus, basically confined to Tehran’s expat community, and moving within the privileged lifestyle of Iran’s highly educated, English-speaking elite.
Little did we know that a political storm was brewing that would soon disrupt our world, turn it upside down, and banish our Iranian friends from their homeland.
We were under the reign of the Shahanshah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi, Iran’s last king who left Tehran with his family at the peak of the 1978-79 revolution to go on self-exile.
Tehran was then a bustling city that reflected the Shah’s efforts to modernize the nation.

It is no secret that Pahlavi was restored to power in a 1953 coup d’etat staged by the U.S. and Great Britain to stave off moves to nationalize the country’s oil industry that was dominated by the British-controlled Anglo-Iranian Oil Company.
Pahlavi had taken over his father, Reza Shah, who started their dynasty in 1925 but abdicated in 1941 after the Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran during World War II.

The younger Pahlavi was forced to briefly leave Iran in the face of protests and political pressure after he tried – and failed – to remove the widely popular Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh and his nationalist policies.
The British and U.S. intelligence services then launched Operation Ajax, a covert plot that toppled Mossadegh and placed the Shah back in his palace with Western backing.
Of course, I knew none of this in my happy-go-lucky world then.
In 1967, Mohammed Reza Pahlavi crowned himself as the Shahanshah, the King of Kings.
His third and last wife, Faribah Diba, ascended to become the Shabanu or Empress.
In time, their eldest son, then seven-year-old Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi, was to inherit the Peacock Throne from his father.
My parents, especially my mother, was impressed by the pomp and pageantry of the monarchy.
I remember her gushing when she brought us to the museum to gawk at the crown jewels that rivaled those of the British royal family.

But the Shah was an absolute ruler who implemented economic, social and political reforms in what was called the White Revolution intended to modernize (read Westernize) and industrialize his country – and strengthen the monarchy.

Notably, the reforms granted Iranian women the right to vote, run for public office, afford greater access to education and employment, and encouraged them to shed their hijab (head scarf) and chador (a cloak, usually black, covering the body from head to toe).
Although many still wore their hijabs and chadors even in the more progressive capital, we – Iranians and foreigners both – never did, mindless of the disapproving stares from conservative locals.

Somewhere in the blurry background of my teenage years, I would hear vague stories about Mossadegh and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini who were said to have both been thrown out of Iran for opposing the Shah.
Adults whispered about the supposedly dreaded SAVAK, the Shah’s powerful and brutal secret police.
In time, I began to see what I learned were protest messages scrawled on public walls in Persian script that I could not read and never really paid mind to.
It was not part of my reality.
As it turned out, many Iranians disapproved of the White Revolution.
They felt the Shah was abandoning national traditions, destroying Islamic values, and making the country too dependent on the West and its values.
Land reform was not working (farmers were given small plots, lacked water, tools, and access to credit), forcing people in rural areas to move to the cities.
Poverty increased as wealth and development benefited only the urban elites.
On the political front, opposition parties were restricted as activists and religious figures were sent to prison or into exile.

Opposition and anger at the Shah grew even stronger in 1971 when he hosted a four-day festival to celebrate the 2,500 th anniversary of the founding of the Persian Empire by Cyrus the Great estimated to have cost up to $10 million.

Some 1,200 kings, queens and other royals, heads of state, and government leaders from all over the world, including then first lady Imelda Marcos, attended the five-and-a-half-hour banquet held at a tent city with luxurious accommodations built near the archaeological ruins of Persepolis.
I remember my mother led preparations for a welcome ceremony held by the Filipino community in Tehran for Marcos when she arrived for the festival.
Mama even had clueless me recite a poem or welcome remarks for the occasion.

Furious Iranians regarded the festival, which included military parades depicting Persian history and the inauguration of the iconic Shahyad (Memorial to the Shah in Farsi, renamed Azadi Tower), as excessively extravagant, elitist, and ignored social realities in the country.
These growing grievances fueled the mass protests that eventually overthrew Pahlavi and ended the monarchy.

text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Bea eventually included her daughter Victoria Hope, whom she fondly calls Hopea, in the interaction.
The three of them briefly appeared together and smiled at the camera.
However, Bea's own comments made the nature of the reunion clear: she and Meray are not co-parenting.
Their appearance together was specifically for the vlog and the engagement it could generate.
The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope.
Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple.

passages.text: Bea Borres and her former boyfriend Meray Yamada recently appeared together in a candid clip, but she made one thing clear from the beginning: their reunion does not mean they are co-parenting their daughter, Victoria Hope.
The former couple’s unexpected interaction was featured as a “bonus clip” in Bea’s latest vlog, which she later reposted on Facebook and quickly caught the attention of netizens.
READ: Bea Borres reveals the face of her daughter Hope: ‘Too beautiful to not share’ Before bringing Meray into the frame, Bea immediately gave a disclaimer behind their reunion.
“I’m still not co-parenting, okay?” she maintained.
Bea then candidly admitted that she decided to film with Meray partly because their interactions tend to generate strong engagement online.
“I’m doing this because kailangan kong pumaldo,” she said, joking that if even one clip from their reunion becomes trending, she could use it to create more content.
Among the content ideas she suggested were a co-parenting vlog and even a lie detector test challenge.
When Meray finally appeared, Bea continued to make light of the situation while referencing their difficult past.
“Nandidilim na naman ‘yung paningin ko, naririnig ko na siya...You know why I’m doing this?
Because you don’t want to give me money.
Eh malakas ‘yung engagements pag kasama ka eh.
Gagatasin na lang kita.
You ruined my peace when I was pregnant,” she told him.
READ: Bea Borres bares stretch marks to promote body positivity and empower fellow moms Bea also joked about Meray supposedly having other women and teased that their video might make them jealous.
Meray, however, denied the claim.
“I don’t have babae,” Meray responded.
The playful exchange continued as Bea had Meray taste a cake she had baked herself.
Since he was on a diet, she gave him several spoonfuls.
When Meray asked if the cake contained poison, Bea jokingly replied: “Sana nga eh.”
She later offered him another bite while teasing: “Para mag-away kayo ng babae mo.”
Meray admitted that their reunion was unexpected and that he had no idea what Bea had planned.
Bea then revealed that she intentionally kept the vlog's concept from him so he would not have the chance to decline.
“Pag kumita ‘to, gagatasan kita because you don’t want to give me money,” she said, once again joking about turning their interaction into more content.
But amid the playful exchange, Bea reiterated that their appearance together should not be mistaken for a change in their arrangement.
“We’re not co-parenting and I’m still not going to co-parent with you after this...for the video lang. Know your place,” she said.
Bea eventually included her daughter Victoria Hope, whom she fondly calls Hopea, in the interaction.
The three of them briefly appeared together and smiled at the camera.
She then asked her followers if they wanted to see more videos featuring both of them.
“Hashtag cloutchaser. Hashtag this guy does not want to give me money,” Bea joked.
Meray also had a brief interaction with their daughter during the vlog, with Bea being vocal about not wanting Hopea to call Meray as her “daddy.”
Their unexpected reunion naturally prompted mixed reactions from viewers.
Some found their playful exchanges entertaining, while others admitted feeling kilig seeing the former couple together again.
However, Bea's own comments made the nature of the reunion clear: she and Meray are not co-parenting.
Their appearance together was specifically for the vlog and the engagement it could generate.

READ: Bea Borres gives daughter Hope her last name: ‘one of the proudest moments of my life as a woman’ During her interview with Boy Abunda in May, Bea revealed that they had attempted to live together for their daughter but eventually realized that their arrangement was not working.

“Tito Boy, I tried. Pinakita ko, nagsama kami, nag-acting kami na para kaming pamilya. Pero bumalik lahat ng sakit. When I was pregnant, wala talagang anything tapos ngayon, kahit sabihin ko na 'ayoko, ikaw mag adjust for me' nag-expect pa rin ako na he would try. Nakalabas na daughter namin, pero wala talaga,” Bea said.
She also explained that Meray’s mother has been involved in caring for their daughter.
When Tito Boy asked whether she is co-parenting with Meray, she gave a straightforward response: “I’m co-parenting with his mom.”
In another interview in 2025, Bea said that she and Meray had been together for only about a month when they found out she was pregnant.
At the time, she said their relationship was already “kind of rocky,” and they eventually separated before she publicly announced her pregnancy.
The vlogger-mom gave birth to Hopea in December last year.
Reflecting on her strength and confidence as a single mother, Bea decided for Hopea to carry her mother’s surname, as seen in her daughter’s certificate of live birth posted last January.
Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content.
In a YouTube vlog titled "Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno," Bea inserted a short clip toward the latter part of the video, where she let Meray try the cake she baked.
According to Bea, she purposely included Meray in the vlog to drive online engagement, which could then generate income.
The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope.
“I’ll just milk him for all he’s worth,” Bea said in Filipino.
“You don't want to give me money? Well, engagement is high whenever I'm with you, so I'll just milk this for all it's worth,” she added.
In the video, Bea spoon-fed Meray some of the cake she made, which she said could cause a fight with his other women.
“You ruined my peace when I was pregnant, and you have a lot of women, so this act is for you to fight with them since karma takes so long to catch up,” she said.
Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025.
That same month, she shared a sonogram and revealed that she is having a baby girl .
In January, Bea revealed that she had given birth to Victoria Hope, or Hopea , in December 2025.
In August, she returned to school at the Ateneo de Manila University .
—Hermes Joy Tunac/JCB GMA News
Content creator Bea Borres breaks her silence amid the mixed reactions to her reunion with her ex-boyfriend Meray Yamada.
Recently, the celebrity mom met up with Meray for what she jokingly described as a "clout-chasing" move for her vlog.
Bea also playfully said that reuniting with her ex would help her earn money for their daughter, Victoria Hope.
Despite their apparent boundaries, however, some fans still felt the kilig vibes between the former couple.

Others, including Bea's close friend Andrea Brillantes, disagreed with the netizens' excitement over the ex-couple. READ: Andrea Brillantes on Bea Borres-Meray Yamada ship: 'Lahat kayo kinikilig, pwes ako hindi' Amid the reactions, Bea shared her thoughts on the hate comments circulating online.
"Why are you guys mad at me!," she wrote.
"Atleast I'm not accepting online sugal 😒 Mag clout chase nalang ako 😒 It's my content, just block me nalang if you think i'm tanga!!!!"

The influencer also added in the comments, "If I promote sugal diba you'll bash me rin naman, go kanya-kanya na 'tong hustle." The following day, Bea Borres continued sharing content featuring Meray. Titled "Gatasan Serye," the new video showed Bea and Baby Hopea watching Meray play basketball.
The influencer noted how much her daughter enjoyed cheering for her dad, while she continued to maintain her playful distance from her ex.
Despite their recent posts together, Bea previously clarified in their vlog that she and Meray will not be co-parenting as a couple.
READ: Bea Borres not worried taking on responsibility as a single parent Bea Borres previously revealed that they had broken up before she publicly announced her pregnancy last year.
She gave birth to Hopea on December 15, 2025, and brought her daughter home in January after a 44-day stay in the NICU.

Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Content creator Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother. Borres was the guest on the May 8, 2026 episode of "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" which served as a Mother's Day special ahead of May's second Sunday. A majority of the episode revolved around Borres laying out her pregnancy experience, including how she and Yamada got together as well as how they broke up while carrying their child. Boy asked Borres if she was co-parenting with Yamada, whom the content creator humorously referred to as her "baby daddy," and Borres answered Yamada's mother Imelda "Mhel" Pechera was co-parenting with her. "Wala akong masabi kay Tita. Tita, if you're watching, napakabait mo... pero 'yung anak mo talaga..." Borres quipped. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? I'm just choosing myself, the way he chose himself," she pointed out. The episode ended with the titular "Fast Talk" segment after Borres prayed her daughter grows up God-fearing, kind, grounded, healthy, and successful in life, and for herself the ability to heal. — Video from GMA Network's YouTube channel RELATED: Never force: Elisse Joson advises fellow moms to let kids open up naturally Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. articles.text: CEBU, Philippines — Nagkita pag-usab atubangan sa camera ang aktres ug content creator nga si Bea Borres ug iyang ex-boyfriend nga si Meray Yamada alang sa usa ka online content. Sa YouTube vlog nga “Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno,” gipakita ni Bea ang mubo nga video clip diin iyang gipatilaw si Meray sa hinimo niya nga cake.Suma pa ni Bea, gituyo niyang ilakip si Meray sa vlog aron madugangan ang online engagement ug mokita siya niini.Aduna na’y anak sila Bea ug Meray nga ginganlan og Hope . Gipasidunggan ni Negros Occidental 3rd District Rep. Javier Benitez ang Pinoy talents sa global stage, lakip na ang P-pop groups nga BINI ug SB19. Gihimo ni Benitez ang pagdayeg atol sa iyang pakigpulong sa mga kawani sa House of Representatives sa niaging adlaw, isip kabahin sa pagtimaan sa Philippine Creative Industries Month. Giawhag usab sa magbabalaod ang mga personnel sa Kamara nga suportahan ang lokal nga musika. Miangkon ang OPM singer nga si Jed Madela nga nabantayan na niya ang kakapoy samtang nag-perform sa entablado tungod sa iyang pagkatigulang. Matud niya, naningkamot siya karon nga maminusan ang timbang ug mahimong mas aktibo aron mapadayon ang iyang kusog sa pag-perform. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? text.preview: Sinabi kamakailan ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos na ang kanyang pamahalaan ay “mananatiling nakatuon sa pagtiyak ng transparency at mabuting pamamahala, kalayaan sa pagpapahayag at ng pamamahayag, at proteksyon ng mga media practitioner at kanilang mga karapatan sa pagsasagawa ng kanilang propesyon.” Sa pagsasalita sa ika-50 anibersaryo ng Kapisanan ng Mga Brodkaster ng Pilipinas noong Abril 27, binanggit ni Marcos na ika-147 ang Pilipinas sa World Press Freedom Index noong 2022. Nangako siyang “pagbubutihin ang kasalukuyang kalagayan” ng media. Sinabi ng Reporters Without Borders, isang international non-profit organization na nakabase sa France, na ang media sa Pilipinas ay “napakasigla sa kabila ng mga target na pag-atake at patuloy na panliligalig ng gobyerno, mula noong 2016, sa mga mamamahayag at media outlet na masyadong kritikal.” Sa paggunita ngayong taon ng World Press Freedom Day, pinagsama-sama ng VERA Files Fact Check ang mga kaso na inihain laban sa mahigit 90 mamamahayag na Pilipino mula 2007 hanggang 2022. Sa 45 na kaso, 32 ang isinampa ng mga dati at kasalukuyang opisyal ng gobyerno. Tatlumpu’t apat (humigit-kumulang 75%) ang mga reklamong may kinalaman sa cyber libel na mapaparusahan sa ilalim ng Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at ang 10 ay libel sa ilalim ng Revised Penal Code. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. article.title: From monarchy to Islamic rule to war in Iran: A personal account (Part 1)
article.description: I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home.

text.preview: Tress Reyes is senior editor in VERA Files. She also teaches Journalism at UP College of Media and Communication. Flash reports on the bombing of Iran by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 caught me cold that Saturday afternoon. In my mind’s eye, I could picture the devastation even before the initial images appeared on our television in the living room. I grew up in Tehran, Iran. My family moved there in 1968 when I was 10 years old. For over a decade, we considered the country our second home. My father was employed by Iran Airlines, which had hired foreigners to work with and train the country’s own nationals to run the state-owned flag carrier. Papa, who worked at Clark Air Base of the U.S. in the Philippines and Air America in Vietnam, was one of the first Filipino recruits. I lived in Tehran until 1977, when I graduated from high school and returned to Manila to study at the University of the Philippines in Diliman. I remain friends with my former schoolmates at an international school in Tehran who are from Iran, Israel and the U.S., among other nationalities. We were an expat family. The company paid for our third floor flat and tuition for us three children who were enrolled at Community School, where teachers were mostly Americans. We travelled for free or at discounted rates as part of my father’s company benefits. It was a comfortable, carefree life for me that mainly revolved around school and travel to different countries during summer vacations and holidays. We didn’t have a car but had a chauffeur we called Ali Agha (mister), who drove us in his Mercedes Benz. We also had a Russian housekeeper when we were little. The Filipino community in Tehran was small in the beginning. We all knew each other. Our apartment building, like most of the type in the capital, had a garden with roses and a large water fountain. article.title: Bea Borres co-parenting daughter with ex's mother
article.description: Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Content creator Bea Borres is looking after her infant daughter Victoria Hope not with the child's father, Meray Yamada, but the latter's mother. Borres was the guest on the May 8, 2026 episode of "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" which served as a Mother's Day special ahead of May's second Sunday. A majority of the episode revolved around Borres laying out her pregnancy experience, including how she and Yamada got together as well as how they broke up while carrying their child. Boy asked Borres if she was co-parenting with Yamada, whom the content creator humorously referred to as her "baby daddy," and Borres answered Yamada's mother Imelda "Mhel" Pechera was co-parenting with her. "Wala akong masabi kay Tita. Tita, if you're watching, napakabait mo... pero 'yung anak mo talaga..." Borres quipped. The content creator explained she tried to make things work with Yamada, but the recollections of the latter being absent while Borres was expecting just flowed back. "Siguro nage-expect pa rin ako na he would try kasi nakalabas na yung daughter namin, pero wala talaga," Borres continued. "One thing I learned from men is if they really wanted to, they would." Borres acknowledged she had her own shortcomings, latter adding she doesn't see herself becoming friends again with Yamada. "He wasn't there when I was going through the hardest and most vulnerable moment of my life, so bakit ko siya papayagan maging parte ng kasayahan ko ngayon? I'm just choosing myself, the way he chose himself," she pointed out. The episode ended with the titular "Fast Talk" segment after Borres prayed her daughter grows up God-fearing, kind, grounded, healthy, and successful in life, and for herself the ability to heal. — Video from GMA Network's YouTube channel RELATED: Never force: Elisse Joson advises fellow moms to let kids open up naturally Philstar.com is one of the most vibrant, opinionated, discerning communities of readers on cyberspace. article.text: CEBU, Philippines — Nagkita pag-usab atubangan sa camera ang aktres ug content creator nga si Bea Borres ug iyang ex-boyfriend nga si Meray Yamada alang sa usa ka online content. Giawhag usab sa magbabalaod ang mga personnel sa Kamara nga suportahan ang lokal nga musika. output.description: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content.
output.text: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content. In a YouTube vlog titled "Hot Moms Bake with Jam Magno," Bea inserted a short clip toward the latter part of the video, where she let Meray try the cake she baked. According to Bea, she purposely included Meray in the vlog to drive online engagement, which could then generate income. The content creator also clarified that they are still not co-parenting their daughter, Hope. “I’ll just milk him for all he’s worth,” Bea said in Filipino. “You don't want to give me money? Well, engagement is high whenever I'm with you, so I'll just milk this for all it's worth,” she added. In the video, Bea spoon-fed Meray some of the cake she made, which she said could cause a fight with his other women. “You ruined my peace when I was pregnant, and you have a lot of women, so this act is for you to fight with them since karma takes so long to catch up,” she said. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025. That same month, she shared a sonogram and revealed that she is having a baby girl . In January, Bea revealed that she had given birth to Victoria Hope, or Hopea , in December 2025. In August, she returned to school at the Ateneo de Manila University . —Hermes Joy Tunac/JCB GMA News

output.title: Bea Borres says she's co-parenting her daughter with her ex-boyfriend's mom
output.description: Bea Borres gave a tell-all on Fast Talk with Boy Abunda Friday
output.text: Bea Borres gave a juicy tell-all interview on "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" Friday, and among the many things she shared was how she's in a co-parenting setup with... her ex-boyfriend's mom. When Tito Boy asked if her baby daddy is present and if the two were co-parenting, Bea flat-out said, "I"m co-parenting with his mom." Adding she really "tried" to keep him present in their daughter's life, Bea said the effort was just not there. "Tito Boy, I tried. Pinakita ko, nagsama kami, nag-acting kami na para kamig pamilya. Pero bumalik lahat ng sakit," Bea said. "When I was pregnant, wala talagang anything tapos ngayon, kahit sabihin ko na 'ayoko, ikaw mag adjust for me' nag-expect pa rin ako na he would try. Nakalabas na daughter namin, pero wala talaga," she added. Bea took the opportunity to share what she's learned about men, saying, "One thing I learned about men is if they really wanted to, they would." "Kahit anong sabihin kong 'ayoko, 'wag mo kitain anak ko,' pupuntahan niya kasi gusto niya. Dahil anak niya yon. Pero walang ganon," she said. Meanwhile, Bea admitted she tends to nag men, "and ang mga lalake, ayaw yun." "Kelangan ko i-point out yung mistakes niya, and hindi ako mabait. Feeling ko, nasasaktan ko rin siya," she added. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025 and said she will not co-parent with anyone. In December, she gave birth to a baby girl she named Victoria Hope , who spent 44 days in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) before getting discharged. On TikTok last year, Bea revealed her baby daddy was none other than Meray Yamada . They were only together for one month when she got pregnant. — LA GMA News

output.description: Bea Borres explains how she found the perfect name for her daughter.

text.preview: Actress and social media influencer Bea Borres revealed the name of her soon to be daughter for the very first time. In an interview with vlogger Toni Gonzaga, the Kadenang Ginto star shared how she found the perfect name for her first born–– Victoria Hope. Bea announced pregnancy to the public earlier this month to the surprise of her followers. The father of her daughter is her ex-boyfriend who she has already broken up with prior to the announcement. READ: Bea Borres confirms her pregnancy: ‘I’m so happy talaga’ The content creator recalled how her best friend, actress Andrea Brillantes, was the first one to bring up the name Hope as a possible name for her baby in one of their conversations. She shared how both of them were dealing with their own problems at the time. “Si Blythe, she texted me because she was also going through something. Ako naman, umiiyak ako kasi I was going through a breakup tapos she texted me na ‘Bea, sana girl ‘yung baby mo tapos ang pangalan niya ay Hope’,” she recalled. It was the first time that Bea revealed something about her baby as she admitted wasn’t given the opportunity to do so in the past. She was hounded by several rumors about her pregnancy before she even announced it herself–– something she found unfair. “I was at my rock bottom pero I feel like and I know sa mga public na sinabi ko, punong-puno na ako ng hope ngayon. The hope na everything will be okay. Na binigay talaga siya ni God sa akin kasi may reason siya at hindi basta basta lang,” she expressed. “Just because of that text and because of that word, parang na-feel ko na ‘ay may name na siya, so ke-keep ko na to’ and nagkaroon ako ng hope na hindi pa talaga mage-end yung life ko. Mas naging accepting talaga ako, kaya ever since kahit hindi ko pa alam ‘yung gender, Hope na talaga yung name ko for my baby,” she added. output.title: VERA FILES FACT CHECK: This video DOES NOT show parents rallying at Comelec for Makabayan bloc’s expulsion
output.description: It's a composite of four clips showing other protests and events. Neither was held at the Comelec’s office; not one called for the progressive bloc’s expulsion.

text.preview: An 11-minute video uploaded on Nov. 9 by the YouTube channel PH BREAKING NEWS falsely claimed to show parents protesting in front of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) office to get the Makabayan bloc out of Congress. While the League of Parents of the Philippines (LPP) held such a rally in January , this video of PH BREAKING NEWS is a composite of four clips showing other LPP protests and events. Neither was held at the Comelec’s office; not one called for the progressive bloc’s expulsion. articles.text: Bea Borres and her ex-boyfriend, Meray Yamada, reunited in front of the camera for content. articles.title: Bea Borres says she's co-parenting her daughter with her ex-boyfriend's mom
articles.description: Bea Borres gave a tell-all on Fast Talk with Boy Abunda Friday
articles.text: Bea Borres gave a juicy tell-all interview on "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda" Friday, and among the many things she shared was how she's in a co-parenting setup with... her ex-boyfriend's mom. When Tito Boy asked if her baby daddy is present and if the two were co-parenting, Bea flat-out said, "I"m co-parenting with his mom." Adding she really "tried" to keep him present in their daughter's life, Bea said the effort was just not there. "Tito Boy, I tried. Pinakita ko, nagsama kami, nag-acting kami na para kamig pamilya. Pero bumalik lahat ng sakit," Bea said. "When I was pregnant, wala talagang anything tapos ngayon, kahit sabihin ko na 'ayoko, ikaw mag adjust for me' nag-expect pa rin ako na he would try. Nakalabas na daughter namin, pero wala talaga," she added. Bea took the opportunity to share what she's learned about men, saying, "One thing I learned about men is if they really wanted to, they would." "Kahit anong sabihin kong 'ayoko, 'wag mo kitain anak ko,' pupuntahan niya kasi gusto niya. Dahil anak niya yon. Pero walang ganon," she said. Meanwhile, Bea admitted she tends to nag men, "and ang mga lalake, ayaw yun." "Kelangan ko i-point out yung mistakes niya, and hindi ako mabait. Feeling ko, nasasaktan ko rin siya," she added. Bea announced her pregnancy in August 2025 and said she will not co-parent with anyone. In December, she gave birth to a baby girl she named Victoria Hope , who spent 44 days in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) before getting discharged. On TikTok last year, Bea revealed her baby daddy was none other than Meray Yamada . They were only together for one month when she got pregnant. — LA GMA News
